content:
This is a small papercut but keeps showing up: syntax foo := ... takes def-style visibility modifiers private/public, but all other meta helpers like the ordinary syntax command create public meta defs by default and take local to set private visibility.

This leads to confusing errors:

module

syntax foo := "a"

/-- error: unknown parser declaration/category/alias `foo` -/
#guard_msgs in
syntax "b" foo : term

I understand that := makes it a little more "def-like", and so I see the sense behind private/public, but I think having a uniform interface for controlling the visibility of syntax would be worth the trade-off. :) Also, syntax foo := will almost always be used in following syntax definitions, and so should be public meta by default lest we make errors the common case. (And if it were public meta by default, we'd expect a local-governed visibility.)

Concretely, the proposal here is to have syntax foo := ... create a public meta def and use local to create a private meta def. public/private syntax foo := would still parse, and would log informative deprecation messages suggesting the new syntax.

Happy to make a PR if it would help and if this sounds reasonable. :)

Hmm, that's a valid papercut. Indeed it is private instead local because it is an inert def and not some other scoped effect. But that decision was made before the module system and public existed, so I see the sense of preferring consistency with other syntaxes
